name: Mean Reversion
rationale: Mean-reversion rules test whether short-term downside extensions tend to rebound enough to compensate for timing risk and trading costs.
expected_benefit: Potentially improved risk-adjusted return or lower exposure by buying weakness and exiting after recovery instead of staying fully invested.
failure_modes: Catching falling markets where oversold readings keep getting worse.
Small edges disappearing after slippage and commissions.
Strong dependence on the chosen exit rule.

canonical_variants.name: RSI pullback long/cash
canonical_variants.description: Enter long after RSI falls below an oversold threshold and exit when RSI recovers above a neutral threshold.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A daily RSI pullback strategy may improve risk-adjusted return versus buy-and-hold by concentrating exposure after short-term oversold conditions.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe versus buy-and-hold while retaining at least 70% of benchmark CAGR after realistic costs.

suggested_validation: Predefine one RSI length and one entry/exit threshold pair before running.
Compare against buy-and-hold and cash benchmarks.
Run cost sensitivity because turnover may be high.
Run date sensitivity across trending and choppy market regimes.
references: Connors and Alvarez, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work
Academic and practitioner literature on short-horizon reversal effects
execution_notes: The engine can execute simple daily RSI long/cash variants. It does not currently support limit orders, pairs, intraday fills, or volatility-scaled entries for this family.
